llm.summary: This skill is a coherent task-planning helper, but it asks for broad activation and can persist derived records from local task/memory data without tight scope controls.

dimensions.detail: The main purpose, semantic splitting and reusable JSON-based planning, matches the included instructions, references, sample capability JSON, and local json_manager.py script.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md says the skill must trigger for nearly any task request or inferred need, which is broader than a specialized planning skill needs and can steer unrelated user requests into this workflow.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No external dependencies, package installs, network fetches, or opaque install scripts were found; metadata and static scan are clean, and VirusTotal telemetry is null.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The automation reference describes reading recent memory logs and bulk-generating persistent capability/rule JSON; that may be purpose-related, but the artifact does not define clear dataset limits, sensitivity filtering, authorization, or scheduling boundaries.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The script and references support creating and updating JSON artifacts, including user-supplied paths in several CLI commands; this is expected for a JSON manager but under-scoped for an agent-exposed skill because it is not confined to the skill data directories.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review this carefully before installing. It appears aimed at task planning rather than malware, but you should only use it if you are comfortable with a skill that may activate on broad task requests, read recent memory/task logs during automation workflows, and write persistent planning JSON. Prefer running it only with explicit confirmation and constrain any CLI paths to its own data directories.
llm.findings:
[SDI-2] expected: The file read/write behavior is related to managing planning JSON, but the unrestricted input and output paths in json_manager.py are broader than necessary and remain a real containment concern.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad mandatory trigger language in SKILL.md is not necessary for the stated semantic-planning purpose and creates a realistic risk of over-activation in multi-skill environments.
[SQP-1] expected: Automation for consolidating capability/rule JSON is related to the skill, but the reference's memory-log reading and recurring execution are under-scoped and lack explicit user-control guardrails.
